J=\{t:T-t\le\lambda k\},\qquad E=\{j:j\le T-\lambda k\}.

\[
\left|\sum_{j\in E}d_j^{(t)}\right|

\ge Q_E(1-\eta-D)-D-2\eta-2D
\ge \frac14

for all large \(T\), since \(Q_E\to1\) and \(D=O(T^{-1/4})\). Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz therefore gives

\sum_j\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}
\ge \frac{(\sum_{j\in E}d_j)^2}{Q_E}
\ge \frac1{16}.
